query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 5 at.% Boron to the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy will improve its ductility and toughness by 25% and 30%, respectively, relative to the baseline alloy, due to the formation of a boride precipitate phase that enhances grain boundary cohesion and promotes plastic deformation.
generation.conditions: Arc melting and casting, followed by homogenization at 1000°C for 24 hours
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary cohesion enhancement and promotion of plastic deformation
generation.predicted_outcome: 25% increase in ductility and 30% increase in toughness
generation.baseline: As-cast HfZrTi high-entropy alloy without Boron addition
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in ductility and toughness may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and microstructure of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and Charpy impact testing of the alloy with and without Boron addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured improvement in ductility and toughness is less than 10% and 15%, respectively, the hypothesis is falsified
